interpretations: Group by `eventannotm` with NULL as its own group. Compute each group's average `instownpct` (NULLs ignored). Baseline = unweighted mean of group averages. Select groups with average strictly above the baseline. Return one row: the mean of those groups' averages and the mean of (group average − baseline)
Same as 1, but the baseline is computed over only the non-NULL timing groups (Pre-market, Intraday, Post-market). The NULL group is still compared against it and can be included in the result
Same as 1, but the NULL-timing group is excluded entirely: it is not a group, not in the baseline, and not in the result
Same as 1, but the baseline is the average of `instownpct` over all snapshots (each snapshot counts equally). Groups are compared to that overall mean
Same as 1, but a group whose average `instownpct` is NULL (every value missing) is kept as a group. It counts in the baseline denominator as zero, or is dropped from the baseline
Same as 1, but groups whose average `instownpct` is NULL are excluded from the baseline and from the comparison
Same as 1, but "missing timing" also covers empty-string or placeholder values in `eventannotm`, which are merged into the NULL group
Same as 1, but the output has two columns: the mean of the above-baseline group averages, and the mean excess over the baseline. Each is shown as a separate unrounded value
Same as 1, but the output is a single value: the mean excess alone. This is the same as the mean of the above-baseline averages minus the baseline
Same as 1, but if no group is strictly above the baseline (for example, all groups are equal), return one row with NULLs. In the other reading, return zero rows
Same as 1, but "mean of their averages" is weighted by each group's snapshot count rather than counting each group equally
Same as 1, but the average is taken over distinct `instownpct` values within each group, not over all snapshots
Same as 1, but snapshots are joined to `transactionrecord` or `trader` first. Only snapshots with a valid linked transaction are counted, and the grouping is unchanged
Same as 1, but the baseline is the median of the group averages instead of the mean, and groups are compared to that median
Same as 1, but "missing timing" is treated as its own group only when NULL, while empty strings are kept as a separate distinct group (not merged with NULL)
Same as 1, but the mean excess is computed as a percentage or ratio relative to the baseline (average of (group average − baseline) / baseline) rather than as an absolute difference
Same as 1, but groups are compared to the baseline with "at or above" (≥) rather than strictly above
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS a
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  GROUP BY eventannotm
),
b AS (
  SELECT AVG(a) AS base FROM g
)
SELECT AVG(g.a) AS mean_avg, AVG(g.a - b.base) AS mean_diff
FROM g, b
WHERE g.a > b.base;
SELECT eventannotm,
       AVG(infoleaksc) AS avg_infoleaksc,
       AVG(infoleaksc) - (SELECT AVG(infoleaksc) FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE eventannotm IS NOT NULL) AS diff_from_baseline
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY eventannotm;
SELECT eventannotm,
       AVG(infoleaksc) AS avg_infoleaksc,
       AVG(infoleaksc) - (SELECT AVG(infoleaksc) FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE eventannotm IS NOT NULL) AS diff_from_baseline
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
WHERE eventannotm IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY eventannotm;
SELECT corpeventprx, AVG(instownpct) - (SELECT AVG(instownpct) FROM sentimentandfundamentals) AS diff_from_overall_mean
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY corpeventprx;
SELECT corpeventprx
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY corpeventprx
HAVING AVG(instownpct) IS NOT NULL
   AND AVG(instownpct) > (
     SELECT AVG(g)
     FROM (
       SELECT AVG(instownpct) AS g
       FROM sentimentandfundamentals
       GROUP BY corpeventprx
     )
     WHERE g IS NOT NULL
   );
